correctness.rationale: For each initial mixed petal, the first independent rate-one ring makes the pair agree permanently with the then hub opinion. Any initially monochromatic pair retains its color under all subsequent majority updates. Thus after a maximum of finitely many independent exponential times, all pairs are fixed, leaving exactly one two-state recurrent class for each mixed-color petal partition and a singleton for either homogeneous partition. Rates and stationary law follow by counting incompatible locked pairs. An exponential race between opposite-color locked petals and mixed petals proves the conditional consensus probabilities; a binomial identity gives the iid formula. No numerical evidence substitutes for the all-size sample-path proof. The extracted exact-rational standalone script separately checked 2,835 finite-state properties for each configuration up to five petals.

originality.rationale: The published 2023 hypergraph-majority framework specifies the whole-group rule and general adaptive dynamics, but its mean-field and simulation analyses do not present an exact all-size recurrent-class classification or independent-initialization consensus formula for a fixed loose hyperstar. The closest full-text studies of triple majority on modular/tripartite hypergraphs, adaptive hypergraph voting, and spatial block-majority do not imply the explicitly computed loose-star two-state recurrent classes. Multiple scientific-record searches did not identify a same-statement or stronger covering theorem. Absence of an indexed hit is not itself a proof of priority; unindexed equivalents remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named exact analysis of majority rule on a loose three-uniform star could predate this result.
The conclusion does not follow for single-vertex majority updates, a distinct and common convention.
All novelty comparisons are same-model mathematical review, not independent scientific priority adjudication.

value.rationale: This is a natural sparse connected hypergraph benchmark for the primary whole-group majority mechanism. Contrary to heuristic intuition that connectedness encourages eventual global consensus, it has an explicit exponentially large family of recurrent polarized classes and an exponentially vanishing iid consensus probability. The exact all-size recurrent spectrum, arbitrary-state absorption probability, and harmonic leaf-freezing time provide a non-routine structural connection between local group overlap and persistent diversity and are reusable for testing approximations and intervention rules.
